caption: The drawing features a geometric garden layout surrounded by a brown vertical-post fence. The garden is divided into four main square sections, each bordered by light pink pathways. The top left and bottom right sections have symmetrical, blue and green decorative patterns incorporating circular and leaf-like shapes. The top right and bottom left squares contain ornate, pink and green patterns with central circular flower motifs. The bottom left quadrant contains rows of red and brown rectangles, likely representing planted beds. Surrounding the garden on two sides is a green area, with two white structures: an arched entryway on the right side and a triangular-roofed building in the lower right corner. Adjacent to the bottom left corner outside the fence is a blue well with a crank and a hanging bucket. At the top left of the image, a horizontal band features a detailed, monochrome drawing of fruits, flowers, and foliage above a shaded text that reads “FRUITS, FLOWERS AND VEGETABLES FROM VAN DER DONCK’S VOYAGES... 1642.” In the lower right corner outside the garden, the text “The Stuyvesant Garden from the Castello Plan 1660” is written in blue script near a blue stamped seal. The overall color palette includes shades of green, pink, blue, brown, white, and beige.
title: Peter Stuyvesant Garden
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
